breaking_news.headline: Toy company CEO shares how Trump's new round of tariffs could affect business
breaking_news.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Jay Foreman of toy importer Basic Fun! about President Trump's latest round of tariffs. The company has paid millions of dollars in import duties under Trump.

breaking_news.headline: Kalshi attacks a Wisconsin law banning election bets as 'voter suppression'
breaking_news.summary: The spat between the leading prediction market company and a key battleground state could be a glimpse into the next major fight between states and the fast-growing industry.

breaking_news.headline: Yes, it's possible to save money while paying off credit card debt. Here's how
breaking_news.summary: In fact, experts recommend it because it can keep you off the hamster wheel of debt. Here's how to find the money in your budget to put toward savings and credit card payments.

breaking_news.headline: AI tokens could become the kilowatt-hour of the AI age
breaking_news.summary: AI companies use tokens to track usage and bill customers. Now economists are using them to track the spread of AI through the economy.

breaking_news.headline: As many are priced out of buying, the renter-owner wealth gap is wider than ever
breaking_news.summary: Record high housing costs have pushed the wealth gap between renters and owners wider than ever. It's been a boon for owners even as many others are priced out.

breaking_news.headline: FIFA has a new plan to raise billions of dollars: Selling stakes in the World Cup
breaking_news.summary: FIFA has a complex plan to sell chunks of its commercial rights to the World Cup to minority investors, including a firm run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Jared Kushner.

breaking_news.headline: A divided Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady despite high inflation
breaking_news.summary: The Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rate unchanged Wednesday.  Fed policymakers say they remain committed to curbing stubborn inflation.

breaking_news.headline: More Americans are going bankrupt. What does that mean?
breaking_news.summary: The bankruptcy rate has risen about 48% between 2022 and 2025, although it's still below pre-pandemic levels.

breaking_news.headline: More than 100 aftershocks hit Japan after powerful quake that killed 13
breaking_news.summary: People are being urged to stay alert, with earthquake aftershocks potentially reaching magnitude 7, officials say

breaking_news.headline: Oscar-winning songwriter Glen Hansard killed in crash
breaking_news.summary: Hansard, who was 56, won the best song Oscar for the 2007 low-budget musical film Once.

breaking_news.headline: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina
breaking_news.summary: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over their behaviour after their World Cup final loss to Spain and throughout the tournament.

breaking_news.headline: Four women accuse Jared Leto of criminal sexual conduct
breaking_news.summary: The actor and musician faces allegations from 10 women in total who say he mistreated them as teenagers.

breaking_news.headline: France fire crews battle heat as locals tell BBC of fight to save homes
breaking_news.summary: "It's our forest," one volunteer fighting the fire in the Gironde region told the BBC, as other locals have refused to heed evacuations.

breaking_news.headline: Zendaya on working with Tom Holland in Spider-Man: ‘When you’re best friends it’s easy’
breaking_news.summary: The couple walked the white carpet at the London premiere of their latest film, Spiderman: Brand New Day.

breaking_news.headline: Two firefighters die in Crete as wildfires threaten parts of southern Europe
breaking_news.summary: Gale-force winds have whipped up the flames prompting the evacuation of several villages on the island, as parts of the continent also continue to tackle fires.

breaking_news.headline: Saudi Arabia's dilemma as it tries to stay out of US-Iran war
breaking_news.summary: The kingdom faces a choice of whether to keep hitting back as a deterrent or to try to de-escalate the situation.

breaking_news.headline: Data centres could pay hundreds of millions in deposits for power demands
breaking_news.summary: The regulator said a fee of between £237,500 to £712,500 per megawatt should be charged for upcoming projects.

breaking_news.headline: Andy Burnham wants to fix social care - what are the options?
breaking_news.summary: With Andy Burnham saying he wants to bring "substantial change" to social care in England, BBC Verify looks at what could be done.

breaking_news.headline: 'Don't wait until you want revenge' - why prenups are on the rise
breaking_news.summary: More young couples are now signing prenups to set out who gets what in the event of divorce.

breaking_news.headline: Matcha and protein pivot pays off for Greggs as profits rise
breaking_news.summary: UK's largest fast-food chain says it is changing its menu "in line with changing tastes and trends".
